description: 6 exemplars (one German) + 3 near-misses + 2 counterexamples. Authored 2026-10-13 under road-to-skill-scripts-that-run-where-they-land, which rewrote this skill's grounded chart-type invocation to the bundled `node <skills-root>/…/ground.mjs` form and so brought it into check_routing_coverage's touched-skill scope. Exemplars are the four decisions its own procedure owns — which signals a dashboard should carry, which surface it belongs on (Grafana / app / embed), the RED-USE-Golden-Signals layout, and the per-panel visualization and threshold choice. Near-misses are three neighbours that share observability vocabulary and answer a different question: the query and JSON behind a panel (grafana), the component that renders an in-app dashboard (livewire), and which of those signals earns a page (alerting-doctrine). Counterexamples guard two words this skill does not own on their own — a 'Dashboard' nav label and a solar 'panel' datasheet.

queries.q: we need a dashboard for the checkout service — which panels and which signals?
should this live in Grafana or as an admin screen inside the app?
lay out the ops dashboard — RED for the HTTP layer, USE for the queue workers
which visualization for p95 latency per endpoint, and where do the thresholds sit?
embed the existing Grafana latency panel in the Laravel admin page — is that the right surface?
wir brauchen ein Dashboard für den Checkout-Service — welche Panels und welche Signale?
write the PromQL for the error-rate panel and save the dashboard JSON
build the Livewire component that renders this admin metrics table
queries.note: the component, not the dashboard design → livewire

queries.q: which of these metrics deserves to page someone at 3am?
queries.note: same signals, the paging question → alerting-doctrine

queries.q: rename the 'Dashboard' item in the marketing site navigation to 'Home'
the solar panel supplier changed their datasheet columns — update the importer
